A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Memory Decoder research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial deletions and reformatting in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-modeling, domain-adaptation, downstream-task, question-answering and latency experiments, with additional ablations and in-context learning results in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original perplexity, downstream-task, cross-model, cross-vocabulary and latency results, alongside empirical analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The cached kNN supervision, self-retrieval exclusion, hybrid KL/language-modeling objective, parallel inference and probability interpolation remain unchanged. Cross-tokenizer adaptation still reinitializes the embedding and output layers. Newly specifying WikiText-finetuned starting models adds implementation information without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 removes Natural Questions and HotpotQA evaluation from Section 5.5, its heterogeneous training corpus from Appendix C, and all 13 biomedical, financial and legal downstream benchmarks from Appendix D. This substantially reduces QA, reasoning and applied task coverage. WikiText-103, the nine general NLP tasks and language modeling on the three specialized domains remain.

E2.justification: The explicit biomedical KL-only and CE-only comparisons in v1 Table 9 disappear, removing the KL-only comparator entirely. The retained benchmark comparisons still use In-Context RAG, kNN-LM, DAPT and LoRA as before. DAPT-model interpolation in v2 Table 7 already appeared in v1 Table 17.

E3.justification: V2 drops the domain benchmarks' zero-/few-shot evaluation protocols and the controlled CaseHOLD comparison using 0, 4, 8 and 16 demonstrations. For retained finance experiments, Section 4 revises the corpus period from April 2024–February 2025 to April–October 2024; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. The retained sliding-window scoring, training budgets and principal evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes the interpolation-parameter sensitivity study across 11 Qwen models, the biomedical ablation testing whether both loss components are needed, and the CaseHOLD analysis of compatibility with in-context learning. The DAPT-interpolation ablation is moved from Appendix E into Section 6.3, rather than newly introduced. Decoder-size, token-case, DAPT-scoring and kNN-distribution analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both use point estimates and the same distribution plots; cross-task and cross-model averages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises GPT2-small DAPT perplexity from 15.74 to 14.76, changing its ranking relative to the unchanged kNN-LM score of 15.62. The decoder-size table changes DAPT from 15.47 to 14.76 and its average from 12.38 to 12.20. Numerous results disappear, including MemDec's 28.01 on NQ and 27.72 on HotpotQA, domain-task scores, and sensitivity, component-ablation and ICL results. Most matched MemDec scores remain unchanged; the relocated DAPT-interpolation results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and equations (1)–(11) retain the same definitions and objectives. The alternative-loss formulas and mathematical discussion move from v1 Appendix H to v2 Appendix D without substantive revision. No theorem or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the same plug-and-play adaptation claim and average perplexity reduction of 6.17 points. The introduction's three contribution statements and the conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval replacement, model compatibility, efficiency and preservation of general capabilities despite reduced supporting experiments.

C2.justification: V2 removes substantial interpretations concerning compositional QA reasoning, complementarity with demonstrations, context-length effects and minimal interpolation-parameter calibration. It also removes the large-datastore latency-scaling explanation and the claimed greater-than-140-fold parameter efficiency. The explicit limitations on training-time retrieval and cross-tokenizer updates, and Appendix B's qualification of DAPT degradation as partly an evaluation artifact, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised future code/checkpoint release with GitHub and Hugging Face collection links. Section 4 newly specifies that both GPT2-xl and the GPT2-small initialization were finetuned on WikiText. Small-model size labels are standardized to 124M from inconsistent 117M/125M descriptions. The removed QA appendix's 722MB corpus composition and dataset-access information disappear. The PDFs establish these documentation changes, not external resource availability or experimental reruns.

R1.justification: V2 removes Geng et al. (2024), Great Memory, Shallow Reasoning, together with the discussion positioning MemDec against kNN-LM's reasoning limitations. The Radford et al. GPT2 citation is also removed. Section 7's broader positioning remains substantially unchanged; consolidated duplicate references and bibliographic restyling do not represent additional research changes.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendix structure are substantially condensed: the QA section and separate corpus, domain-task and ICL appendices disappear, while the DAPT-interpolation discussion is shortened and incorporated into Section 6.3. Front matter, affiliations, acknowledgements and citation formatting also change. Much of the surviving introduction, method and conclusion remains nearly verbatim.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different report layout, including a colored abstract panel, colored headings, running headers and footers, and Figure 1 on the title page. Several tables are removed, and v1 Table 17 moves into the main text as v2 Table 7. All six figure graphics retain identical content, with changes to placement and sizing.

improvement.justification: V2 improves access information, clarifies initialization, makes the DAPT numbers internally consistent and removes some overstated efficiency statements. However, it deletes the QA and 13 domain-task evaluations, ICL analysis, parameter-sensitivity study and direct loss-component ablation without replacement evidence. With the broad adaptation and capability-preservation claims retained, these removals substantially weaken validation of practical transfer and the training objective, outweighing the documentation and presentation gains.
